observed: No audio or video implementation exists: no media transport, signalling, NAT traversal, camera/microphone handling or UI in either SDK. Auth Core implements only the escalation state machine and records a result that the bank gateway reports.
evidence: grep for webrtc|AVCapture|AVAudio|camera|microphone|RECORD_AUDIO|CameraX in SDK sources: 0 hits (only the BIP39 word "video"). docs/integration/bank-backend-guide.md:403 states Auth Core does not verify the assertion.
impact: The intended in-app audio/video confirmation does not exist; any claim of in-app audio/video verification is unsupported.
remediation: Decide build vs. integrate (see 07_AUDIO_VIDEO_AUDIT.md plan): SDK UI module, media transport (WebRTC or provider SDK), session signalling bound to authorizationId + canonicalPayloadHash + credentialId, signed provider results verified by Auth Core.
closure_criteria: Audio and video sessions run end to end inside both demo apps on physical devices; provider result signature verified server-side; negative tests for spoofed, replayed and cross-transaction results.

observed: The AUDIO/VIDEO result is accepted from the bank client (mTLS gateway in production) with any opaque assertion; only its SHA-256 is stored. The session is bound to authorizationId and a nonce, not to the credential or the transaction hash the provider saw.
evidence: Code inspection; e2e step "provider result recorded, plan VERIFIED" passes with an arbitrary assertion string (scripts/e2e-smoke.mjs).
impact: A compromised or faulty bank gateway can mark a step-up factor as passed. The device signature is still required, so this cannot approve a payment alone, but the AUDIO/VIDEO factor in evidence is an unverified statement.
remediation: Define a signed provider-result format (JWS) including sessionId, authorizationId, canonicalPayloadHash, result and time; pin provider keys in Auth Core; reject unsigned results in production.
closure_criteria: Unsigned or mismatched provider results rejected in production mode; tests for wrong session, wrong transaction hash, replayed result.

observed: The biometric prompt text is one line: operation, amount, then all beneficiary values with "name" before "iban", each up to 512 characters, then the reference. No display length limit exists, and blank values are skipped.
evidence: Code inspection of both SDKs and the server limit (512 chars, 16 fields). Not executed on a device: whether iOS/Android truncate the prompt text must be verified on hardware.
impact: A long payee name can push the IBAN out of the visible part of the system confirmation prompt, weakening "what you see is what you sign" in the system UI (the signed bytes and evidence stay correct).
remediation: Cap displayed field lengths (e.g. name <= 70) at server and SDK; put the account identifier first in the prompt; require a full-screen confirmation view built from signed bytes before the prompt; reject whitespace-only values.
closure_criteria: Device tests on supported iOS/Android versions show amount, currency and full account identifier in the system prompt for maximum-length inputs; shared vector added for over-long fields.

observed: The offline code is an HMAC under a key that Auth Core also holds (stored encrypted with DEVICE_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY). Whoever has the database and that master key can compute valid codes for any pending authorization.
evidence: Code inspection; documented in ADR 0003 and in the evidence format (OFFLINE_CODE "is not verifiable by a third party").
impact: Offline confirmations are not non-repudiable and are forgeable by an operator insider with both secrets.
remediation: Limit OFFLINE_CODE by policy (amount ceiling, operation types); move the per-credential offline key into the HSM (or HSM-wrapped key); mark offline evidence distinctly in bank reporting.
closure_criteria: Policy limits enforced and tested; offline key unwrap only inside HSM; documentation of evidential weight agreed with the bank.

observed: The three master keys are plain environment variables, not HSM-wrapped; ciphertexts carry no key identifier and rotation is not implemented (runbook states "Not implemented" for DEVICE_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY).
evidence: Code and runbook inspection.
impact: Leak of the process environment plus a database copy exposes offline keys, push keys and webhook secrets; no way to rotate after suspected compromise without re-enrolling devices.
remediation: Add key IDs to ciphertexts, support a key ring (current + previous), wrap master keys with the HSM/KMS, implement re-encryption job.
closure_criteria: Rotation test: rotate each master key with live data, old ciphertexts still decrypt, new writes use the new key; production posture requires HSM/KMS-wrapped keys.

observed: Both SDKs rely on platform certificate validation only; no pinning option exists.
evidence: grep for pinning/serverTrust/CertificatePinner: no hits. Documented open item NXS-028 (docs/security/threat-model.md:159).
impact: A trusted-but-hostile CA (corporate proxy, malicious profile) can read traffic and capture a single-use BOOTSTRAP token during its 300 s life. Signatures cannot be forged, but enrolment of another device is possible if that device also passes attestation.
remediation: Offer optional SPKI pinning in NEXUSSignConfig (with backup pins) and document rollout.
closure_criteria: Pinning configured in demo apps; MITM test with a user-installed CA fails to connect.

observed: Attestation is verified only at enrolment and recovery. No per-operation App Attest assertion or Play Integrity check, and no runtime jailbreak/root/hooking detection.
evidence: Code and documentation (NXS-025, threat-model.md:158).
impact: A device compromised after enrolment keeps an ACTIVE credential; malware with root can drive the app UI, although keys stay non-exportable and biometric-gated.
remediation: Add per-operation App Attest assertions / Play Integrity standard requests for high-value authorizations; policy-driven credential suspension on failed integrity.
closure_criteria: High-value authorization rejected when a fresh integrity verdict fails; tests with simulated failed verdicts.

observed: Device request replay protection depends on Redis keeping nonces for 2x skew + 60 s. Failover to an asynchronous replica or restore from snapshot can lose nonces; requirements are documented, not enforced.
evidence: Code inspection; open item NXS-021.
impact: Replay of a captured, still-fresh signed device request after a Redis failover.
remediation: Require synchronous replication/WAIT or move nonces to PostgreSQL with a unique constraint; startup check of Redis persistence settings.
closure_criteria: Failover test shows replayed request refused.

observed: The audited tree has no package-lock.json and no .git directory. CI, the Dockerfile and release.yml all require the lockfile. The owner reported green CI and ran run-local.sh (npm ci) successfully, which strongly indicates the GitHub repository has a lockfile this copy lacks. The GitHub repository could not be accessed by this audit (CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE).
evidence: find; CHANGELOG.md:80 ("The lockfile is not part of this candidate"); git status: not a repository; add_repo: GitHub account not linked.
impact: The baseline is not reproducible from the audited tree; container build and CI fail on it as is; findings may not apply 1:1 to the GitHub head.
remediation: Commit the reviewed lockfile; run this audit against a clone of the GitHub head (record commit SHA); compare the trees.
closure_criteria: Audit rerun on a commit SHA; lockfile present; npm ci and docker build succeed from a clean clone.

observed: The PKCS#11 adapter was not executed: SoftHSM2 could not be installed (no network to the Ubuntu archive), so the HSM suite (10 tests) was skipped. No evidence of a test against a vendor HSM exists in the repository.
evidence: Integration run: "PKCS#11 HSM adapter on SoftHSM2 # SKIP SOFTHSM2_MODULE and SOFTHSM2_UTIL are not set".
impact: Evidence sealing in production mode is unverified in this audit and untested on real hardware.
remediation: Run the HSM suite on SoftHSM in CI (already configured) and on the target vendor HSM; document the key ceremony.
closure_criteria: HSM suite green on SoftHSM and on the bank HSM model; key ceremony record.

observed: No Swift toolchain here; the iOS SDK and the demo were not compiled. The demo project has never been built successfully anywhere (the owners Xcode session on 2026-10-12 stopped at signing because the iPhone was not detected). Secure Enclave, Face ID and App Attest behaviour is untested on hardware.
evidence: Tool check (swift/xcodebuild missing); conversation evidence of the Xcode signing screen.
impact: iOS behaviour, including the strict parser and prompt display, is unproven.
remediation: Build in CI (jobs ios-sdk, ios-demo) and on the Mac; run on a physical iPhone; record results.
closure_criteria: swift test green; demo installed on a physical iPhone; enrolment, signature VERIFIED, recovery on device recorded.

observed: No Android SDK here. The SDK was compiled against hand-written API stubs and its JVM tests ran: 30 of 34 passed; 4 SecurePush tests failed because the kotlinx.serialization stub is not implemented (harness limitation). The demo APK was never built. Keystore, StrongBox, BiometricPrompt untested on hardware.
evidence: Log run/logs/android-jvm.log ("Tests run: 34, Failures: 4"; NotImplementedError in stub json.kt:18).
impact: Android behaviour on devices is unproven.
remediation: Run testDebugUnitTest and assembleDebug in CI; run on physical devices with and without StrongBox.
closure_criteria: CI android-sdk and android-demo jobs green; on-device enrolment and signature recorded.

observed: Expiry is applied only when a confirmation is attempted. GET /v1/authorizations/{id} and the device view keep returning state PENDING_USER after expiresAt; there is no sweeper job and no webhook for expiry.
evidence: Executed 2026-10-16: authorization created with expiresInSeconds=30; GET 33 s later returned state PENDING_USER with expiresAt in the past. Code: no job or query sets EXPIRED outside confirmAuthorization/transitionTerminal.
impact: Bank systems that rely on state rather than expiresAt can treat an expired request as pending; dashboards and audits show stale states.
remediation: Report EXPIRED in read paths when now >= expires_at, add a periodic sweeper and an authorization.expired webhook.
closure_criteria: Test: GET after expiry returns EXPIRED; sweeper transitions rows; webhook delivered.

observed: server.close() is not awaited; the HSM, pool and Redis are closed and process.exit(0) runs immediately, so in-flight requests are cut.
evidence: Code inspection.
impact: Requests in progress during a rolling deploy fail (transactions roll back, so no integrity loss), with client-visible errors.
remediation: Await server.close with a drain timeout, stop accepting new requests, then close dependencies.
closure_criteria: Test: SIGTERM during a slow request completes the request.

observed: NEXUS ID allocation is check-then-insert; a concurrent collision on the same random candidate raises 23505 on the primary key, which is reported as DuplicateBankCustomerError. No check digit.
evidence: Code inspection (catch maps every 23505 to duplicate customer).
impact: Rare misleading 409 for a valid new customer; typing errors in a 9-digit ID are not detectable.
remediation: Distinguish the constraint name and retry on ID collision; consider a check digit for operator-entered IDs.
closure_criteria: Unit test with forced collision retries and succeeds.

observed: The demo bank issues BOOTSTRAP tokens, and on ACTIVE_CREDENTIAL_EXISTS automatically REPLACEMENT tokens, to any unauthenticated caller of its device port. The README exposes that port on the Wi-Fi network (portproxy 0.0.0.0:8443 + firewall rule).
evidence: Executed 2026-10-16: with a device enrolled, an unauthenticated POST /app/bootstrap-token returned a token and the demo log shows "replacement BOOTSTRAP token issued".
impact: Anyone on the same network can enrol or replace the demo customers device while the demo runs. Demo only; must never hold real customer data.
remediation: Bind the demo device port to a pairing code shown on the operator page; warn in README; remove portproxy/firewall rule after the demo.
closure_criteria: Bootstrap requires the pairing code; README warning present.

observed: AUDIO and VIDEO are treated as available unless the bank sets audioAvailable/videoAvailable=false. A push timeout then escalates to a channel the bank may not operate, and the authorization cannot complete.
evidence: Code inspection; docs state the default (bank-backend-guide.md:373).
impact: Stuck authorizations for banks that do not configure the flags.
remediation: Default to unavailable, or make availability a per-client setting at registration.
closure_criteria: Test: client without AV configured never escalates beyond PUSH.

observed: Evidence times come from the server and database clocks. No trusted timestamping (RFC 3161) or external anchoring.
evidence: Code inspection.
impact: An operator controlling the clocks can misstate when an approval happened; order within a chain remains provable.
remediation: Optional RFC 3161 timestamp per record or per periodic checkpoint; NTP monitoring.
closure_criteria: Timestamp token verified by verify-evidence.mjs.

observed: Removing records from the end of a chain is detected only if the verifier gets the head the bank stored (--expect-head). Without it a truncated export verifies. Nothing in the product stores or anchors heads outside Auth Core.
evidence: Executed: truncated export without head -> exit 0; with bank head -> exit 1 "records missing at the end of the chain".
impact: Tail truncation by a database administrator is undetectable unless the bank keeps heads.
remediation: Deliver heads in webhooks (already in confirmation response) and provide a reference bank-side checkpoint store or periodic signed checkpoint published outside Auth Core.
closure_criteria: Integration guide mandates head storage; test bank fixture stores heads; audit procedure uses --expect-head.

observed: Base images referenced by tag, not digest.
evidence: File inspection; open item NXS-040.
impact: Non-reproducible images; silent base changes.
remediation: Pin by digest and update through Dependabot.
closure_criteria: Dockerfiles use @sha256 digests.

observed: No gradle/verification-metadata.xml; dependency checksums are not verified (wrapper JAR is validated in CI).
evidence: File inspection; open item NXS-039.
impact: Supply-chain substitution of Maven artifacts is not detected.
remediation: Generate verification-metadata.xml with checksums and signatures.
closure_criteria: Build fails on a modified dependency.

observed: Release pipeline produces only the Auth Core image, SBOM and provenance. No SDK publishing (Swift Package tag, Maven artifact), no signed SDK artifacts, no demo app distribution.
evidence: Workflow inspection.
impact: Banks cannot consume versioned, integrity-protected SDK releases.
remediation: Add SDK release jobs with checksums/signing and provenance.
closure_criteria: Tagged release publishes SDK artifacts with provenance.

observed: Outdated comment: device endpoints "authenticated by their own short-lived, customer-scoped tokens" (they use device signatures since rc.2). ANDROID_KEY_SECURITY_POLICY has two consecutive docstrings.
evidence: File inspection.
impact: Misleads reviewers.
remediation: Update comments.
closure_criteria: Comments match behaviour.

observed: No performance or load tests; no test runs two Auth Core instances against one database/Redis (workers use SKIP LOCKED, chains use advisory locks).
evidence: grep for k6/artillery/autocannon/benchmark: none.
impact: Capacity and horizontal-scaling behaviour unknown.
remediation: Add load tests for authorization create/confirm and evidence sealing with HSM latency; two-instance integration test.
closure_criteria: Documented throughput and latency targets met; two-instance test green.

observed: No coverage measurement. In this environment coverage could not be attributed (tests transpile TypeScript at runtime).
evidence: Coverage run reported only transpiler files.
impact: Unknown untested code paths.
remediation: Add c8/nyc over dist with source maps; publish coverage.
closure_criteria: Coverage report in CI artifacts.

observed: Backup/restore and disaster recovery are documented only; no test or script exercises a restore of PostgreSQL with evidence chains and HSM key continuity.
evidence: Repository inspection.
impact: Recovery after data loss unproven; evidence chain continuity after restore unknown.
remediation: Scripted restore drill including verify-evidence over restored chains.
closure_criteria: Restore drill report.

observed: Migrations have no down scripts; rollback procedure is not tested.
evidence: migrations/README.md ("None has a down script").
impact: Failed upgrade requires restore from backup.
remediation: Document and test rollback-by-restore per release.
closure_criteria: Rollback drill recorded.

observed: No third-party notices file for bundled open-source dependencies and the BIP39 word list.
evidence: Repository inspection.
impact: Licence compliance for distributed SDKs/images not documented.
remediation: Generate THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES from SBOMs.
closure_criteria: Notices file present for every distributed artifact.

observed: npm registry access is blocked in this environment; dependencies used here were assembled from git sources with stub @types packages. npm audit, Trivy and gitleaks were not run in this audit.
evidence: npm install: 403 from egress proxy; npm ls shows @types/*@*.9999 stubs.
impact: Known-vulnerable dependency versions cannot be excluded by this audit.
remediation: Rely on CI security.yml results for a recorded commit, or rerun with registry access.
closure_criteria: security.yml green for the audited commit, results archived.

observed: Metrics are behind the gateway mTLS check only; any client with a valid gateway certificate (any bank system) can read them; open in development.
evidence: Code inspection.
impact: Operational information disclosure to other bank systems.
remediation: Serve metrics on a separate port or require an operations role.
closure_criteria: Metrics not reachable from bank client routes.

observed: Offline key material reaches app process memory on both platforms. Android: a software EC key pair in memory at enrolment, and the derived HMAC key passes through the heap before import into the Keystore (afterwards the key stays in the Keystore). iOS: the ECDH runs with the Secure Enclave key, but SecKeyCopyKeyExchangeResult returns the shared secret to the app at every offline confirmation (after the biometric prompt).
evidence: Code inspection (Android behaviour documented in the class comment).
impact: Malware with access to the app process memory can capture the offline key: once at enrolment on Android, at each use on iOS. Online signatures are not affected.
remediation: Android: Keystore ECDH (PURPOSE_AGREE_KEY, API 31+). iOS: zero the shared secret and derived key after use; document the residual exposure.
closure_criteria: Keystore agreement on API 31+; secrets wiped after use; device test.

observed: Top-level descriptions list "Push -> Audio -> Video" without stating that NEXUS-SIGN contains no audio/video implementation and that results are bank assertions (stated only deeper, in bank-backend-guide.md:403).
evidence: Documentation inspection.
impact: Readers can infer an in-app audio/video capability that does not exist.
remediation: Add one sentence at both places pointing to NXS-019.
closure_criteria: Wording updated.

observed: Canonical form is sorted-key JSON.stringify, not RFC 8785. Safe today because every signed field is a string and the key set is fixed; any future numeric or nested field needs a new protocol version.
evidence: Code inspection; shared vectors (5 valid, 22 invalid) pass in Auth Core; mobile parsers not executed here except Android JVM.
impact: Future protocol changes could introduce cross-language disagreement.
remediation: Keep the type restriction in the spec; add vectors for each new field.
closure_criteria: Spec states the restriction; vectors cover it.

observed: Control, format and separator characters are refused, but confusable characters (homoglyphs, mixed scripts) and whitespace-only values are allowed.
evidence: Code inspection.
impact: A payee name can imitate another one visually.
remediation: Optional confusable/mixed-script check for name fields; refuse whitespace-only values.
closure_criteria: Vectors with mixed-script names rejected or flagged.
